Definition: to set in a row, i.e. arrange, put in order (in a very wide variety of applications)
BiblicalUsage: To set in order, to arrange in a row, is the word for laying the wood on the altar, laying the pieces of the offering on the fire, setting the battle in array in the valley of Elah, and ordering a cause before God. It is the same careful arranging, whether the thing set in order is wood, an offering, an army, or an argument.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God is a God of order, and setting things in order before Him is itself an act of worship. Abraham laid the wood, the priests laid the offering, and Job laid out his case, each trusting that what is set in order before God is heard.
